findings.reason: the section's whole verdict is "imas-efit misses S ⇒ its representation is implicated", so a worker who renders the shell as a torus, or who is defeated by the axis segment, records a miss against imas-efit's representation when the authored geometry was the defect, and that verdict is written into the plan for §9 and sent to another team.
findings.text: s10 authors the shell as "two new iron-boundary elements … the outer surface anticlockwise and the inner surface clockwise", but imas-efit's IronBoundary is a CLOSED path in (R,Z) with R >= 0 (`src/ironBoundary.h:30-34`), and a spherical shell's poloidal cross-section is a half-annulus whose two arcs close only along the axis R = 0 (the prototype does exactly this at `scripts/prototypes/iron_magnetisation/shell.py:47-50`: `buffer(B).difference(buffer(A)).intersection(half)`). Two concentric closed circles, the natural reading of "outer surface / inner surface", are a torus of revolution, whose exact shielding factor is not the sphere formula of §1; and a contour closed along R = 0 puts a segment through the iron that carries a degenerate (zero-circumference) ring current, which the plan neither states nor justifies. The section therefore does not determine the body it measures.

findings.reason: a worker following the stated field list either lands on the file's existing 215 and scores a value the exact S does not describe, or refuses to start on an unset material2Id, and the missing step is one the plan's own done-when depends on.
findings.text: "the iron_core IDS is withheld, and the permeability is constant" does not by itself produce the mu_r = 1000 the done-when scores. With the IDS withheld, `magneticPermeabilities.readXml` is read from the same XML document (`src/tokamakData.cpp:135-136`), and WEST/iron.xml defines one entry, `id="1" relativePermeability="215"`; `IronBoundary::checkData` requires a selectable permeability for BOTH `materialId` and `material2Id` (`src/ironBoundary.cpp:238-247`), and `MagneticPermeabilities::selectMagneticPermeability` throws for an undefined id (`src/magneticPermeabilities.cpp:86`). So the run needs an authored entry at 1000 for the iron side and a second entry for the vacuum side, and the section's list of required fields ("geometry/category, the knotSet and the observationPoints blocks") omits exactly the two material ids that carry this.

§6b adds a magneticPermeabilities entry at 1000 for the boundary's material to select, since with the IDS withheld imas-efit reads permeabilities from the XML and WEST iron.xml defines only id 1 at 215 (0a9c97ee8).
